All new items are open. - **A, sample efficiency (0.75):** an airbench96-style recipe reaches 75.3% in about 8.5 epochs.   - A1a: reproducing the futurebiohackers submission gives accuracy >=0.753 in <=9 s.   - Ways to cut epochs: dirac init (A2), a wider last block with fewer epochs (A3), brightness/contrast augmentation (A4). - **B, per-epoch compute (0.6):** progressive resizing (B1), SiLU instead of GELU (B2), hard-example selection (B3, low prior). - **C, fixed and per-step overhead (0.5):** compiling the whole train step or using CUDA graphs with a fused optimizer (C1), trimming the timed prepare step (C2), batch size 2000 (C3). - **D, noise and margin (0.6):** this sets the acceptance rule. Every feasible run should also get a standing rule check: - prepare resets everything learned. - build touches no real data. - eval runs in eval mode and stays under 5 s for any batch size from 1 to 1024.

added I001, I002, I003, I004, I005, I006, I007, I008; dropped none. So far there's only the no-op baseline: accuracy 0.012, time 0.11 s, not feasible. All compile and CUDA/cuDNN warmup has to happen in `build`. added I009, I010, I011, I012, I013; dropped none. I added five ideas, which brings the queue to seven. Nothing was dropped: none of the queued hypotheses is settled yet. **Where things stand.** The current best is still E001 at 7.22 s with accuracy 0.7549. That clears the 0.753 bar by only about 0.19 pp, and E003–E005 showed that small recipe changes alone move the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp. **What this means for the ideas.** E004 showed the GPU sits at its 400 W power cap, so only cuts to GPU work shorten training. The main lever is therefore fewer epochs: one epoch is about 0.85 s, roughly 12% of the run. Fewer epochs need extra accuracy from somewhere, so most of the new ideas aim there. **New ideas, in priority order:** - **Priority 5:** Rerun the current best recipe at 8.0 epochs with no other change. If it stays at or above 0.753 it becomes the new best; either way it measures how much accuracy one epoch buys, and it is the baseline for the next two ideas. - **Priority 4:** Add light brightness/contrast jitter at 8.0 epochs. This tests H1.4.1 against that baseline. - **Priority 3:** Lower label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2 at 8.0 epochs. The reference settings were tuned at 8.5 epochs and may leave accuracy on the table at shorter runs. - **Priority 2 (explore):** Use a fused optimizer and compile the optimizer step together with the EMA update. I expect less than the 2% gain H3.1.1 predicts, which would confirm the power-cap explanation. - **Priority 2 (explore):** Selective backprop, which tests H2.3.1. From epoch 3, only the 614 highest-loss images in each batch of 1024 get a backward pass; the run measures the accuracy cost per second saved. **Kept in the queue:** - I007 (train at 24 → 28 → 32 px over the run) fits the power-cap finding well. - I008 (batch size 2000) is now lower value. E004 suggests that removing per-step overhead does little on this GPU, so I didn't add more ideas of that kind. **Not added:** I left out a Muon optimizer test (H5.1.1) because it is unlikely to cut time.

Changes to the hypothesis tree, following the results, literature search and skeptical review: **Supported** - **H1.1 / H1.1.1:** E001 and E002 replicate exactly (0.7549, 7.22 s). I removed the claim about the ResNet9 template, which was never measured. - **H4.1 / H4.1.1:** reworded to cover what E002 actually showed: accuracy is identical for a given seed and time noise is ~0.1–0.5%. It says nothing about accuracy noise. **Refuted** - **H1.3:** making group 3 wider adds about 10% cost per epoch (E005, plus the reference ablation). - **H2.2:** switching GELU to SiLU cost 0.61 pp, about 2.6 times the noise level, at fixed hyperparameters. - **H3.2:** prepare is about 1% of time, and E004 cut it with no effect on the score. **Retired** - **H1.2 / H1.2.1:** the reference recipe already uses dirac init, so the premise is false. **Downgraded** - **H3 (overhead) to 0.2, with H3.1 and H3.3 at 0.2:** E004 suggests the GPU runs at its power cap, so cutting CPU or launch overhead barely changes time. **Restated** - **H2.1** now requires the low-resolution stage to be at least 26 px (24 px leaves a degenerate final pooling map), a crop or antialiased-resize operator, and a real full-resolution phase at the end. - **H2.1.1** stays inconclusive because E006 changed several things at once. - **H4** now uses perturbation noise (~0.23 pp standard error on the 3-seed mean) and calls for a mean of about 0.756 or more, or checks on extra seeds. - **H1** is lowered to 0.5, since E006 shows cutting resolution trades better than cutting epochs. **New hypotheses** - **Under H1:** measure accuracy against epoch count locally (8.0 epochs predicted at about 6.8 s). - **Under H2:**   - The power-cap mechanism (time tracks GPU energy), tested by logging power and clocks.   - E006's accuracy loss comes from its 24 px stage and random-resized crops. Two tests: 26 px with antialiased downsampling, and crop mode against resize mode.   - Narrowing groups 1 and 2, where most of the FLOPs are. - **Under H2.1:** a schedule with 40% at full resolution, and a check that E006's augmentation randomness follows the trial seed. - **New Lvl1 (N_free):** accuracy gains that cost no time, which can then be spent on epoch or resolution cuts. Two tests: decay the learning rate to 0 instead of 0.07x, and re-estimate BN statistics at 32 px after progressive resizing. - **Under H4:** perturbation noise and the risk of picking a variant that is only lucky on seeds 0–2. Two tests: the spread across three neutral changes, and A1a's accuracy on extra seeds 3–10. Priorities: progressive resizing with the confounds removed, the epoch slope, and decaying the learning rate to zero. Muon (H5), selective backprop (H2.3) and CUDA graphs (H3.1) go last.

Expected -3 to -4% time for a loss of up to about 0.3 pp. - **Priority 2, H7.2:** bs 2048 in the 16/24 px phases only, where Muon's fixed per-step cost is the largest share of epoch time. **Explore (about 1/3):** - **Priority 3, H4.3.1:** a determinism ablation. If seed 0 then reproduces bit for bit, later comparisons can be paired by seed, roughly halving decision noise. - **Priority 2, H7:** move the classifier head to Muon. I brought the tree in line with the evidence, the review and the search. **Status fixes against the pre-registered bars:** - Supported: H7.1.1 (E030) and H7.2.3 (E038, confirmed by the rerun E039). - Refuted: H7.1.2 (E034), H7.2.1 (E035: time saving too small) and H6.3.1/H6.3 (E037). - Retired: H7.2.2. The E033 spectrum analysis shows that 3-step Polar-Express coefficients are already worse than the fixed ones, so 2 steps would be worse still. - H5 keeps its refuted status. Its E020+/E024+ evidence tokens follow the opposite sign convention, which is noted in the reason; I could not edit the tokens themselves. **Restated hypotheses:** - **H7** keeps its main claim: Muon was the optimizer lever (supported, confidence lowered to 0.55). Its "the hyperparameters still have room" clause is closed. Momentum, LR, Newton-Schulz step count and label smoothing each came back flat, and E035's gain turned out to be noise. **H7.2** now says only cutting the step count reduces Muon's per-step cost. The momentum buffer is too small for an fp16 buffer to save measurable time. - **H2.4** now admits that the power-cap model fails in the 16/24 px phases (E038 saved ~2 ms per removed step). It also records that gains coming from per-step overhead are at higher risk of not carrying over to the 300 W PCIe judging card than gains from cutting FLOPs. - **H2.8** drops the "diminishing returns" claim. Once E026's lucky run is averaged out, the cost per 16 px epoch looks roughly linear. E041 is re-read as inconclusive rather than refuted. - **H2.10** and H2.10.1 are lowered. The measured costs make "move epochs to 16 px and spend the savings on more 32 px training" roughly break-even or worse. - **H4** now uses E038/E039 as a second rerun pair, notes that its noise estimate rests on only n=2 pairs, and flags that the seeds 3-10 margin check has not been redone on the bs 1536 tip. - **H4.2** is supported: E040 replicated E029 almost exactly, and E035's apparent gain disappeared. **New hypotheses:** - **N1:** per-phase batch size (fast.ai, OLMo), with N1a (bs 2048 at low resolution, 1024 at 32 px) and N1b (bs 3072 at low resolution after a short small-batch start). - **N2:** CUDA-graphing the step for the low-res shapes only (N2a), gated on N2b, a per-phase CUDA-event timing under H2.4. - **N3/N3a:** warmup retune at ~256 steps. - **N4/N4a:** LR floor under Muon. - **N5/N5a:** a group-2 width retest under Muon (a FLOP-reducing lever). - **N6:** seeds 3-10 margin check on the E038 tip. - **N7:** the unbundled determinism probe. - **N8:** an offline check of AOL preconditioning before any scored run. **Suggested order before any further cuts:** 1. Run N6, N7 and H2.4.1/N2b, which are cheap and untimed. 2. Confirm whether E038's parent commit includes E035's renorm change. 3. Run N1a, the most promising lever. Open Lvl1 hypotheses: H2, H4, H6.
